outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 4 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other/Supervisor/Director/Treasurers and Controllers titles), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first

entry_target_review.note: Civil, Transportation and Water/Wastewater Engineers are all direct entry roles.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A park needs a 6 m long timber footbridge, 1.5 m wide, carrying a pedestrian live load of 4 kPa plus its own dead load. Prepare a calculation package for the two main beams: load takedown, maximum bending moment and shear, required section modulus for a stated allowable bending stress, deflection check against span/360, and a short note on what a full design would also check (lateral stability, connections, durability, local code requirements). Show units throughout.

rubric.description: Tributary width, load combination and moment and shear for a simply supported beam are calculated correctly.
Section is sized from the section modulus and checked for deflection with a stated modulus of elasticity.
Identifies the remaining checks and that the design must follow the governing code and be reviewed by a licensed engineer.

reference_answer_outline: Each beam carries half the deck: live load 4 kPa times 0.75 m plus dead load estimate.
Uniform load w; moment w L squared over 8; shear w L over 2.
Required section modulus equals moment over allowable stress; select a glulam or sawn size.
Deflection 5 w L to the fourth over 384 E I compared with 6000/360 mm.
Other checks: bearing, connections, lateral torsional buckling, vibration, preservative treatment.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. The city proposes converting a four-lane arterial into two travel lanes, a center turn lane and bike lanes (a 'road diet'). Neighbors are worried about traffic backing up. Prepare a 10-minute presentation outline for the public hearing: the problem the project addresses with crash and volume data (use clearly invented example figures), maps or diagrams you will show, expected effects on travel time, how you will answer the three most likely objections, and how public comments will be recorded and answered.

rubric.description: Presents crash, speed and volume data in understandable visuals with honest labeling of estimates.
Anticipates objections (congestion, emergency access, business deliveries) with evidence-based answers.
Explains next steps and how comments influence the decision.

reference_answer_outline: Slides: existing cross-section and proposed cross-section diagrams, corridor map with crash locations.
Data: daily volume within the range where road diets usually work, crash history by type.
Expected travel-time change at peak hours from a traffic model, with uncertainty.
Answers on emergency vehicles using the center lane, loading zones, and a monitoring period.
Comment cards and an online form; responses published before the council vote.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A small town water utility produces 2.0 million liters per day but bills customers for only 1.5 million. Write a technical report (executive summary and four sections, about two pages) on the water loss: a water balance using the standard categories of real and apparent losses, likely sources in this system (with invented but plausible figures), the field and data work needed to confirm them, the costs and savings of three reduction options, and a recommended plan.

rubric.description: Breaks non-revenue water into real losses (leaks, main breaks) and apparent losses (meter error, unbilled use) with consistent numbers.
Specifies how losses will be confirmed (district metering, acoustic leak detection, meter testing).
Options have costs, savings and payback, and the recommendation follows from them; the summary is understandable to the town council.

reference_answer_outline: Non-revenue water 0.5 million liters per day, 25 percent of production.
Split estimate: leakage, customer meter under-registration, unbilled authorized use such as flushing.
Field work: night flow analysis, acoustic survey, testing a sample of old meters.
Options: leak detection and repair, meter replacement, pressure management; cost and payback each.
Recommendation and a monitoring indicator for annual reporting.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You are the owner's field engineer on a two-story school addition, and tomorrow the contractor pours the second-floor concrete slab. Create the pre-pour and during-pour inspection checklist: items to verify against drawings and specifications (rebar size, spacing, cover, embedded items), concrete delivery and testing checks, site safety items, what you photograph and record, and what you do if you find nonconforming work an hour before the pour.

rubric.description: Items reference the design documents and include measurable checks (bar size and spacing, cover, slab thickness, mix ticket).
Includes fall protection, shoring and formwork checks, and field testing of concrete (slump, temperature, cylinders).
Defines a clear authority and procedure for stopping or delaying the pour and documenting the issue.

reference_answer_outline: Rebar per drawings, chairs for cover, laps, openings and embedded conduits in place.
Formwork and shoring inspected; edge protection; access routes.
Delivery tickets: mix design, time since batching, water added; slump and air tests; cylinders made per specification.
Daily report with photos, weather, crew counts.
If nonconforming: notify the contractor and engineer of record, issue a written notice, re-inspect before pour proceeds.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A developer submits plans for a 220-unit apartment complex with one driveway onto a two-lane collector road near an elementary school. Write the city's traffic impact review memo: estimate weekday peak-hour trips using a stated trip-generation rate (cite the source type you would use and label invented rates), distribute trips to the network, identify intersections and pedestrian routes to check, list conditions of approval you might require, and note what you would ask the developer's consultant to revise.

rubric.description: Uses a stated rate per unit for AM and PM peaks, shows the arithmetic, and distributes trips reasonably.
Considers school pedestrian routes, sight distance at the driveway and turn-lane needs.
Proposes specific, justified conditions or study revisions rather than general concerns.

reference_answer_outline: Rate assumption such as about half a trip per unit in each peak hour, giving roughly 110 peak trips.
Distribution by direction based on the street network and destinations.
Check the driveway, two adjacent intersections and the school crossing.
Conditions: left-turn lane if warranted, sidewalk connection, crosswalk improvements, sight-triangle clearance.
Ask for counts taken when school is in session and a queuing analysis.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A growing town of 30,000 people expects summer demand to exceed its well capacity within six years. Develop a water efficiency program plan as an alternative or complement to drilling a new well: baseline demand by sector (invented but labeled figures), four efficiency measures (for example, irrigation scheduling, fixture rebates, tiered pricing, leak repair), estimated savings and cost per unit of water saved for each, an implementation timeline, and how you would measure actual savings.

rubric.description: States baseline demand by sector and a savings target linked to the capacity gap.
Each measure has estimated savings and cost per unit saved so they can be compared with the cost of a new well.
Savings are measured against weather-normalized baseline data, not assumed.

reference_answer_outline: Baseline: residential indoor, outdoor irrigation peak, commercial, and losses.
Measures: smart irrigation controllers, rebates for high-efficiency fixtures, seasonal tiered rates, leak repair program.
Cost per cubic meter saved for each versus the new well's cost.
Phased timeline over three years with outreach.
Monthly billing data compared with a weather-normalized baseline; annual report to council.
